name: Kimre
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: OLAC resources for Kimré (kqp), www.language-archives.org/language/kqp (Wayback snapshot 2026-05-12).
sources.note: No language-description items at all (only Crúbadán, Glottolog, Ethnologue, LINGUIST List pointers); no SIL archive items.

sources.citation: Newman, Paul. 2013. Online Bibliography of Chadic and Hausa Linguistics, Version-02 (ed. D. Löhr). Indiana University ScholarWorks.
sources.note: Bibliography only; searched full text: no entry mentions Kimre/Kimré at all (Tobanga, Gabri, Nancere, Lele entries exist).

sources.citation: Dono, Eric Edjinaïn. 2025. Typologie des adjectifs en kimré. Relecture d'Afrique 2(6), octobre 2025: 85-107.
sources.note: Nothing. Morphosyntax of adjectives only; data transcribed in IPA with H/L tone marks (e.g. gùrɔ́ wónù 'cet arbre'); p.101 'Il porte toujours le ton haut' of the interrogative /mí/, /yóóng/. p.86: author states no prior scientific work exists on Kimré ('aucun travail scientifique n'a été effectué sur elle').

sources.citation: Dono, Éric Edjinaïn. 2025. La pluralisation des noms en gabri bordo : étude morphologique d'une langue tchadique du sud du Tchad. Akofena n°17, vol. 4 (sept. 2025): 279-290.
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent. Describes lexical H/L tone schemes (bas-bas, bas-haut, haut-haut) and tonal changes marking noun plural (p.284-285); Bordo = Buruwa (Bordo), listed by Ethnologue 15 as a Kimré dialect, same location (dép. de Manga, Tandjilé).

sources.citation: Peust, Carsten. 2018. The subgrouping of East Chadic. Folia Orientalia 55: 235-253.
sources.note: Nothing; Kimre is not among the 16 East Chadic languages treated (checked full text).

sources.citation: Gordon, Raymond G. (ed.) 2005. Ethnologue, 15th ed., entry Kimré [kqp] (Wayback snapshot 2007-08-23).
sources.note: Nothing; gives dialects Kimruwa (Kim-Ruwa, Kimré), Buruwa (Bordo), Tchire (Tchere-Aïba); alternate name Gabri-Kimré.

sources.citation: Chan, Eugene (ed.). Numeral Systems of the World's Languages: Kimré (data from Amos & Heather Oumounabidji, 1989). lingweb.eva.mpg.de/channumerals/Kimre.htm
sources.note: Numerals only, untoned; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Dono, Eric Edjinaïn. Further articles / doctoral work on Kimré (ENS Bongor; e-mail edjinaindonoeric@gmail.com), e.g. a phonological sketch announced implicitly by his 2025 documentation programme.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only linguist currently publishing first-hand Kimré data; a phonology paper by him would be the primary source for a stress/tone statement.

sources.citation: Vanderkooi, Mark, William Chesley & Jean Doun. 1990. Rapport d'une enquête sociolinguistique entre le Gabri du Nord (Tobanga) et le Gabri du Sud (Dormo/Darbe). SIL Tchad, 28 pp.

sources.note: SIL survey covering the Gabri cluster incl. Kimré wordlists; survey reports occasionally note tone/stress in the wordlist phonology remarks.

sources.note: Only Glottolog reference with Jungraithmayr's own field observations on the Zweistromland languages incl. Kimre; may contain a line on tone/accent typology of the Nancere-Gabri group.

sources.citation: Caprile, Jean-Pierre & Herrmann Jungraithmayr. 1973. Inventaire provisoire des langues 'tchadiques' parlées sur le territoire de la République du Tchad. Africana Marburgensia 6(2): 31-48.

sources.citation: Jungraithmayr, Herrmann. Unpublished Kimre field notes (Zweistromland surveys 1972-1976), Frankfurt/Marburg; cf. the Jungraithmayr & Peust series publishing these notes (Kwang 2023, Gadang 2022, Sarwa 2021, Saba 2020).

sources.note: If a Kimre instalment of the Jungraithmayr & Peust 'précis de grammaire' series appears (Folia Orientalia / ZDMG), it would be the first phonological sketch and would state tone/accent explicitly.
